'''Louis Welles Shapiro''' (born 1941)<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Shapiro, Louis W.|url=https://viaf.org/viaf/114739103/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Virtual International Authority File}}</ref> is an American mathematician working in the fields of [[combinatorics]] and [[finite group theory]]. He is an emeritus professor at [[Howard University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=People {{!}} Howard University Department of Mathematics |url=https://mathematics.howard.edu/people |website=mathematics.howard.edu}}</ref>

Shapiro attended [[Harvard University]] for his undergraduate studies and then the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] for graduate school.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=41506|title=Louis Welles Shapiro|website=Math Genealogy Project|language=en-US}}</ref> Shapiro is most known for introducing the [[Riordan array]], named after mathematician [[John Riordan (mathematician)|John Riordan]],<ref>Louis W. Shapiro, Seyoum Getu, Wen-Jin Woan, Leon C. Woodson,
The Riordan group,
Discrete Applied Mathematics,
Volume 34, Issues 1–3,
1991,
pages 229–239,
ISSN 0166-218X,
https://doi.org/10.1016/0166-218X(91)90088-E.
</ref> and developing the theory around it.  He has been an organizer of and speaker at the annual International Conference on Riordan Arrays and Related Topics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tsimf.cn/meeting/show?id=169|title=6th International Conference on Riordan Arrays and Related Topics|website=6th International Conference on Riordan Arrays and Related Topics |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/view/5rart/home?authuser=0|title=5th International Conference on Riordan Arrays and Related Topics|website=5th International Conference on Riordan Arrays and Related Topics |language=en-US}}</ref> which has been held annually beginning 2014.
